source: English translation: Valmiki Ramayanam, IIT Kanpur (https://www.valmiki.iitk.ac.in/), via the MIT-licensed Valmiki Ramayan Dataset by Ashutosh Vijay.

verses.1: Seeing Sita crying there, the hermit boys ran to where the revered Valmiki, of keen intellect, resided.
verses.2: Having saluted the feet of the great sage, the hermit boys reported to him everything about her crying.
verses.3: O venerable one, this woman, never seen before, the wife of some great soul, cries out with a distorted face as if Lakshmi herself were deluded and wailing.
verses.4: O venerable one, please observe carefully this excellent woman on the river bank, who appears distressed as if a goddess has fallen from the sky.
verses.5: We have seen her weeping profusely, intensely overcome by grief, alone and miserable like an orphan, though she is undeserving of such sorrow and grief.
verses.6: Indeed, we do not believe her to be a human woman, so let proper hospitality be offered to her, as she has come seeking refuge with you near the hermitage.
verses.7: The virtuous woman desires a protector, O venerable one, and you ought to protect her; having heard their words, the knower of dharma, who had gained spiritual sight through asceticism, ascertained the situation with his intellect and rushed to where Maithili was.
verses.8: The great sage Valmiki, perceived by his disciples as he was departing, proceeded a short distance on foot towards a particular spot.
verses.9: Having taken a beautiful offering, Valmiki arrived at the bank of the Ganga and there saw Sita, Rama's beloved wife, appearing helpless and unprotected.
verses.10: The foremost sage Valmiki spoke sweet words to that Sita, who was afflicted by the burden of sorrow, as if comforting her with his spiritual radiance.
verses.11: Valmiki addressed Sita, saying, "You are the daughter-in-law of Dasharatha, the beloved queen of Rama, and the daughter of King Janaka; welcome to you, O chaste wife."
verses.12: Valmiki further stated, "You, as you were coming, were known to me through my meditation on dharma, and indeed, all the reasons for your arrival have been discerned by my heart."
verses.13: O highly fortunate one, your true nature is indeed known to me, and everything that exists in the three worlds is also known to me.
verses.14: O Sita, I know you to be sinless through the eye of wisdom gained by my penance; O Vaidehi, be confident, for you are now under my protection.
verses.15: Not far from my hermitage, there are female ascetics engaged in penance, and they, O dear child, will always protect you as a mother protects her calf.
verses.16: Accept this offering, confident and free from distress, and do not feel any sorrow, as if you have come to your own home.
verses.17: Having heard the supremely wonderful words of the sage, Sita, with folded hands, bowed down to his feet with her head and said, "So be it."
verses.18: Sita, with folded hands, followed the departing sage from behind.
verses.19: Seeing the sage approaching with Vaidehi, the wives of the sages, filled with joy, came forward and spoke these words.
verses.20: "Welcome to you, O best of sages; your arrival is after a long time; all of us salute you, please tell us what we should do."
verses.21: Having heard their words, Valmiki spoke this: "This is Sita, the wife of the wise Rama, who has arrived."
verses.22: "She is the daughter-in-law of Dasharatha and the chaste daughter of Janaka; though sinless, she has been abandoned by her husband and must always be protected by me."
verses.23: Indeed, may you all regard her with supreme affection, and especially, let her be worthy of your reverence out of respect for my words.
verses.24: And having repeatedly entrusted Vaidehi, the greatly renowned and great ascetic Valmiki, surrounded by his disciples, returned to his own hermitage. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 49 ।। Thus ends the forty-ninth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
